name: Handing Off to Kindergarten
title: Handing Off to Kindergarten
answer: Handing off to kindergarten means preschool teachers prepare a short, careful profile of each child so the kindergarten teacher begins the year with useful knowledge. It matters because the move to kindergarten is one of the biggest transitions in a child's life, and good information can make it smoother. Screening results can also shape early practice, but the aim is a confident start rather than an early test.

sections.body: This idea is a structured handoff from preschool to kindergarten. A preschool teacher drafts a short profile for each child that covers strengths, interests, current goals, and what helps the child feel settled. The kindergarten teacher then starts the year already knowing something about each child. The problem it solves is the information gap at a major transition, where a new teacher may otherwise begin without the knowledge the preschool teacher has. AI can help prepare the draft, but the content is about the child and must be handled with care.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In the preschool to kindergarten band, the preschool teacher drafts the profile and the kindergarten teacher receives it before the year begins. The profile describes strengths, interests, current goals, and what helps the child feel settled. Screening results can shape the first weeks of kindergarten. If a spring screener shows a child needs more practice with letter sounds, the teacher can use an approved tool to create short practice activities for the summer or the first month. That practice should be playful and brief, and a teacher should review it.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no study, figure, or evidence label for this idea. It presents the handoff as practice, not as a research finding. The only stated basis is the claim that the move from preschool to kindergarten is one of the biggest transitions in a child's life and that good information can make it smoother. So this idea rests on practice rather than research.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: Names come out during drafting and go back in only in the final version stored in the district's own system. The profile should describe what the child can do and what helps, not labels that could follow a child unfairly. Families should see the profile and have a chance to add to it. A teacher should review any practice activities made with an approved tool. The goal is a confident start, not an early test.
